entries.title: The one-coordinate calculation does not establish the claimed induction
entries.locator: arXiv:math/0410155v1 electronic reprint, Theorem1.1 proof, section2 pp.7–9: restriction B=A minus {z} before(2.5), formulas(2.6)–(2.13), then substitution B=empty. Extracted PDF read17 November2026; no visual-PDF or journal-text comparison.
entries.claim: The two-atom calculation is used to assert(2.5) for arbitrary B, after which B=empty gives the three-function inequality.
entries.problem: The displayed calculation applies when the conditioned fibre has one coordinate. The extension to arbitrary fibres is not proved. ICQP gives the exact tower identity: the averaged conditional E3 plus E3 of conditional means must be supplemented by a sum of covariances between conditional pair covariances and conditional means. That sum can be negative: for independent fair X,Z, f1=f2=X OR Z, f3=Z, conditioned on Z, it is -1/16. This example does not refute the claimed final inequality; its E3 is5/32.
entries.correction: Retain the valid one-bit calculation and the full conditional identity ICQP. A general conclusion requires an additional argument. BXP2 proves all orders for nonnegative Boolean cumulations under product measures; LGXD proves the three-function inequality for bounded nonnegative commonly monotone functions on a product of two chains. Neither replacement supplies the claimed unrestricted theorem. Lieb–Sahi2107.09838v2 Introduction also reports essential gaps; only the discrete step is independently diagnosed here.
entries.leanImpact: A future formal proof must retain the extra covariance terms or provide a different induction invariant. Do not infer global E3 positivity from fibrewise positivity and increasing conditional means alone. The cumulation theorem requires explicit nonnegative Möbius coefficients and a product law; the two-chain result has only two independent ordered coordinates. No compiled association, source confirmation or current resolution of the general conjecture is claimed.

resolution.summary: Proved replacements cover Boolean cumulations and two-chain monotone functions.
resolution.impact: The unrestricted higher-correlation theorem still lacks the missing conditioning argument; the replacements have narrower scope.
